notes: Applied strictly in this order: numeric_brackets -> patterns -> brackets_unwrap -> chars -> NFKD fallback -> whitespace cleanup -> unknown-char audit. Phrase-tier entries MUST precede any char-tier entry for the same codepoints they contain (verified empirically: unicodedata NFKD decomposes superscript/subscript digits to bare digits and MICRO SIGN to Greek mu, not to a spoken word, so superscript digits and MICRO SIGN must be resolved by the phrase/char tiers before the NFKD fallback ever sees them). This table is a starting point meant to grow: when a run hits an uncatalogued non-ASCII character, the skill shows it to the user (codepoint, name, context) and asks before adding a new rule here.

numeric_brackets.notes: bare numeric footnote/citation markers, e.g. [12] -> dropped, not unwrapped (a stray floating digit mid-sentence is worse than the bracket)

patterns.notes: covers both MICRO SIGN U+00B5 and GREEK SMALL LETTER MU U+03BC variants
MUST precede the single section-sign char rule below, or '§§ 60.18, 60.19' reads as 'section section'

brackets_unwrap.notes: strips [SOB], [App], [Protocol], [Approval], [Notice], [Hearing Notice]-style bracket-citation shorthand, keeping the enclosed text. Disable with --keep-brackets. Length-capped and newline-excluded so it can't eat an unrelated multi-line block on a stray bracket mismatch.

chars.name: MICRO SIGN
chars.notes: fallback only; the µg/m³ phrase pattern above should normally consume this first

chars.name: GREEK SMALL LETTER MU
chars.notes: NFKD decomposes MICRO SIGN into this; must be caught here or it survives as non-ASCII

chars.name: SUPERSCRIPT TWO
chars.notes: fallback for bare superscript-two not caught by the word-plus-superscript pattern

chars.name: SUPERSCRIPT THREE
chars.notes: fallback for bare superscript-three not caught by the phrase tier

chars.name: DEGREE SIGN
chars.notes: fallback for bare degree sign not caught by the Fahrenheit/Celsius patterns

chars.name: RIGHT SINGLE QUOTATION MARK
chars.notes: defense-in-depth: -f markdown-smart stops pandoc from injecting curly quotes, it does not un-curl a quote the author typed directly into the source
